Hi Team,
Thanks all for coming together to discuss the slope conditions this week. As discussed, here are our preliminary notes from the meeting. I have included text notes below and the Temporary measures discussed graphically on the sketch. Please review my written notes below and on the exhibit and propose revisions to help us all get quickly towards a final design direction to be finalized/priced out.

At the site visit, we discussed:

Temporary:

* Raising gravel bags along perimeter fence higher than as current
* Adding pylons to support the gravel bags
* Adding rows of gravel bags along property line
* Rows of gravel bags to direct water to the gulley
* Tarp to protect the gulley from widening and taking more soil
* Jute Netting and hydro seed on the majority of the slope and over the recent pipe replacement disturbance area
* Hydro seed on the slope between the concrete gutters
* Tarping off the over steep portions at the top of slope
* Raising the CMP outlet tower above the existing grade
* Adding a curb to direct water from the AMC overflow away from the top of slope
* Installing irrigation to regularly irrigate slope and irrigate hydro seeds

Permanent:

* Soil Nail solutions for steep areas and around the gulley

Complications/challenges:

* Installing mesh netting around existing vegetation
* Gravel bags along fence with little to support them
* how to protect/pin edge of tarp to not allow water under tarp
* Hydro seed may not have enough time to fully grow depending on when rain begins
* Maximizing the amount of temporary work that is permanent

Due to space and terrain limitations no more than 36” rootball trees could have been planted which is what is seen in the photo. And they were spaced apart 30’ or more due to City recommendations
*

*
If this is feasible, we would like to explore this through Guillermo (CREST) for any permitting requirements.
*
The penetrations in the TECCO mesh will be kept at a minimum to accommodate similar size trees that are already planted, - 3’ dia and ~ 30’ apart.

Structural and Josh will need to work together with HCC for the 3’ tall semi-circular retention methods to avoid erosions at these penetrations points where trees will be planted.
*
Landscape will be looking at plug planting for this slope through the Tecco mesh for quicker plant establishment and ground coverage to avoid surface run-offs.
